category_title: Preschoolers who struggle with sharing objects during collaborative tasks
minimal_context: Darin and a friend are using different materials to build a castle together during a 10-minute center time activity.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Darin and Alex, please use these different materials to build a castle together.

STUDENT: (Takes blocks from Alex's pile) Give me that.

TUTOR: Alex is asking for a block to help build.

STUDENT: I had that first.

TUTOR: Remember to share your materials so you can finish the castle.

STUDENT: (Hides the blocks behind his back) That's mine!

options.A: Focus on building rapport so Darin feels safe during the 10-minute center time activity, ensuring that structure, visual cues, predictability, and consistency are prioritized throughout the daily sessions.
options.B: Help Darin understand the relationship between his 'fight' responses and anxiety during the 10-minute center time activity, and frame these reactions into positive coping strategies for future collaborative tasks.
options.C: Target increasing Darin’s ability to share objects with friends to above 60% of observed intervals during one 10-minute center time activity daily, then develop a new goal to continuously share throughout 80% of the specified intervals.
options.D: Establish boundaries and social expectations for safety and respect during the 10-minute center time activity, while targeting executive functioning skills such as planning, decision making, problem solving, and evaluation.
